paragraphs.source_en: Indexing vs. active management is always a fascinating debate; at least for us stock geeks with nothing better to do. Over the decades I’ve been on both sides of it. For a very long time I laughed at the indexers. I made all of the arguments, and then some. After all, if you just avoided the obvious dogs you’d do better than average, right? As we saw in the last chapter, it’s not that easy. But in the summer of 1989, I was still convinced I could win this game.

units.source_en: But in the summer of 1989, I was still convinced I could win this game.

paragraphs.source_en: On a flight back from a business trip, I happened to sit next to a guy who worked for an investment research firm. By the time the flight landed he had suggested I should join them and, at my request, had offered three stock tips. I picked one at random and bought it. Over the next several weeks I watched it triple and by the end of that time I had taken a major pay cut to join the firm in a major mid-career change. Who cared about the salary? The real money would be in the information flow.
